transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, too. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time today. I, well, I want to make sure I'm handling things the right way, so I thought it best to consult a professional. 

I'm dealing with a... a rather difficult situation at my apartment. I don't want to sound like a difficult tenant—I really try to get along with everyone—but for months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been, well, coordinating to pressure me out of the apartment. 

I know how that might sound, but I analyze data for a living, and the pattern is just undeniable. It's subtle things at first... intentionally misdelivered mail, noises in the walls that are timed perfectly to disrupt me, little pointed comments from the neighbors. Whenever I bring it up, they try to brush it off with normal-sounding explanations or show me routine paperwork, but none of that changes the pattern I can clearly see. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly so you don't think I'm just overreacting to normal neighborly things.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory, your ability to focus, or any new physical health problems since these issues with your neighbors began?

Oh, um, no, not at all. My memory is... well, it's as sharp as ever, thankfully. In my line of work, analyzing all that data, you really can't afford to let your focus slip, and I've been keeping up with all my projects just fine. 

I mean, I suppose anyone would be a little... tired, maybe, from the disruptions, but physically I'm in very good health. I make sure to take good care of myself, eat right, that sort of thing. I haven't noticed any new health problems or anything concerning at all. 

Is that... does that answer your question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. I really am trying to handle all of this as reasonably and healthily as possible.
Aside from the noises you hear coming from the walls, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people do not seem to hear?

Oh, no, no, certainly not. I've never heard voices or anything like that. The noises in the walls are just... well, they're just physical sounds, you know? Like thumping or scraping, the sort of things anyone would hear if they were in the room with me. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, imagining things. I assure you, my hearing is perfectly normal, and I don't experience anything out of the ordinary in that regard. It's just the very real, very physical disruptions they're causing. 

Does that... I hope that clarifies things? I want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you accurate information so you can see I'm looking at this logically.
How long has this situation with your neighbors been going on?

Well, um... let's see. It's been about eleven months now. It started shortly after I moved into the new apartment. 

I... I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm just a difficult new tenant who can't adapt to a new building. I really do try to be accommodating, and I spent a long time just observing, trying to give everyone the benefit of the doubt. I didn't want to make a fuss over nothing. But after nearly a year of it, I just couldn't ignore the data anymore. 

Does... does eleven months seem like a reasonable amount of time to wait before seeking a professional opinion? I just want to be sure I'm approaching this the right way, and I certainly didn't want to bother you until I was absolutely certain of what I was seeing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling unusually low or, conversely, feeling exceptionally energetic or irritable during this eleven-month period?

Oh, um, no. My mood has been... quite stable, really. I mean, naturally, anyone would feel a little frustrated when their work is constantly being monitored and interfered with, but I haven't been depressed or anything like that. And I certainly haven't been flying off the handle or acting unusually energetic. 

I try very hard to maintain a professional demeanor, even at home. I think it's important to keep a level head, especially when you're dealing with... well, with a situation like this. I've just been focusing on my analysis and trying to handle it all calmly. 

I hope that sounds like a normal reaction to you? I really don't want you to think I'm overreacting or letting this affect my emotional state. I'm just trying to be as objective as possible about the whole thing.
Do you believe that the people in your building are acting alone, or do you feel that this is part of a larger, more organized effort involving other groups or organizations?

Oh, well... I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm leaping to wild conclusions about, you know, shadow organizations or anything grand like that. I try to stick strictly to the variables right in front of me. I really just think it's... well, it's the property manager and certain individuals right here in the building. It's quite localized, I assure you. 

It's just that for months now, they've been using these very specific tactics. Things like constantly misdelivering my mail, those timed noises in the walls we talked about, and... just little, pointed comments from the neighbors when I walk down the hall. It all seems very clearly designed to pressure me out of the apartment. They've offered paperwork and various administrative explanations, of course, to make it look standard, but... well, no amount of their paperwork or their explanations changes the actual pattern I can see. 

I hope you understand I'm just looking at the data here, as any analyst would. Does that seem like a reasonable way to evaluate it? I'm really not trying to sound like one of those conspiracy theorists, I just... I notice when the pieces don't add up, and I want to be sure I'm explaining it to you rationally.

Have you ever felt that anyone outside of your apartment building, such as coworkers, strangers in public, or people in the media, has been involved in these events or is sending you special messages?

Oh, goodness, no. No, certainly not. I... I know how things like that can sound, people thinking the television is talking to them or that strangers on the street are in on some grand plot. I promise you, I don't experience anything like that at all. That would be highly illogical, wouldn't it? 

My coworkers are entirely separate from this, and... well, strangers are just strangers. As I mentioned, it's strictly confined to the property manager and the building itself. I really try to keep my analysis tied purely to the facts at hand, and I certainly wouldn't let my imagination run away with me to include the media or the general public. 

I hope that helps put your mind at ease about how I'm processing all this? I just want to make sure you see I'm being completely rational about the boundaries of the situation. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality.
Has this situation with your neighbors caused you to miss any days of work, or has it affected your ability to maintain your friendships or other relationships outside of the apartment building?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say it's caused me to miss work in the traditional sense. As an analyst, I have a certain amount of flexibility with my schedule. But... I suppose, to be completely transparent with you—and I really hope this doesn't make me sound unprofessional—I have... well, I've had to pull back from several of my consulting jobs lately. 

It's just that managing this situation properly takes a surprising amount of time. I find myself spending a large part of my week having to follow up with the neighbors, the management office, and the building staff, just to keep everything properly documented and addressed. So, settling into my normal work routine, or even my painting, which I usually do to unwind... well, it's been a bit difficult to find the hours for them right now. 

But I assure you, it's just a temporary reprioritization! I still keep in touch with my friends, and I certainly don't burden them with all these building logistics when we speak. I hope you can see that I'm just trying to handle a very complex situation as responsibly as I can. Does that seem like a reasonable adjustment to make under the circumstances? I'm just trying to be thorough.
Do you believe that the property manager and your neighbors are intentionally trying to cause you harm or distress through these actions?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I really wouldn't use a word like harm. That sounds so extreme, doesn't it? I certainly don't believe anyone is trying to physically hurt me or anything of that nature. I would never make a serious accusation like that... I mean, that would just be entirely unreasonable of me, and I try to be very careful with my words. 

I think it's more about... well, perhaps creating a certain level of distress, yes. Just enough friction and inconvenience to make the living situation untenable, so that I'll simply decide to pack up and leave on my own. It's an administrative tactic, really, rather than outright malice. 

I... I hope I'm making that distinction clear? I'd hate for you to think I'm being overly dramatic or blowing things out of proportion. I'm simply trying to look at their objectives objectively, without taking it personally. Does that seem like a fair way to assess the situation? I just want to make sure my perspective sounds balanced to you.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of these events might be incorrect, or that there could be an alternative explanation for the pattern you are seeing?

Oh, well... I mean, of course. I think any rational person has to ask themselves that question, don't you? I certainly have. I pride myself on being analytical, so naturally, I've tried to look at this from every possible angle. I've asked myself, 'Am I just reading too much into a few misplaced envelopes or some creaky pipes?' 

But... well, I've been tracking this for months now. And I really hope this doesn't make me sound stubborn, because I'm honestly just trying to follow the data. But when you look at the sheer volume of it—the misdelivered mail that always seems to happen right before a lease deadline, the noises in the walls that are perfectly timed to when I'm trying to work, the very specific little comments from neighbors... it just forms a pattern that's impossible to ignore. 

I've tried to accept their explanations, I really have. The property manager has shown me paperwork and tried to brush it off as coincidences or old plumbing, but... well, no amount of their paperwork changes the pattern I can see. It all points to this concerted effort to pressure me out of the apartment. 

I know how that sounds, and I'd really prefer if there were a simpler explanation. I don't want to be a difficult tenant! But I have to trust my own analysis, don't I? I hope you can understand why I feel so certain about this, even though I've tried to be open-minded. Does that make sense? I just want to assure you that I've really, truly tried to see it another way.
